classification.difficultyReason: The first line of the proof is given, and the task tells the student to split the fraction. What remains is index-law simplification: 3^{-2x}/3^{-x} = 3^{-x} and 1/3^{-x} = 3^x. The student then repeats the split for f(x) and compares it with f(-x). This is a routine linked procedure with two small index-law decisions and no open choice of method. It is more demanding than the even/odd checks in p9-q2-block, because those use direct substitution with no manipulation of negative exponents. It is easier than the unscaffolded version of this proof (p10-q7).

classification.difficultyReason: The task is composition of f(x)=x^2-3 with four different g, plus a domain statement for each. Part a is direct substitution. Parts b and d involve a square root that cancels with the squaring, so the student must see that the simplified expression still carries the domain restriction of the inner function. Part c needs the exclusion x≠2 from the reciprocal. The hardest essential demand is the 'simplified form hides the inner-domain restriction' step, which is the same as in p26-q5, whose part is repeated here. It is a step above the plain composition-and-domain parts of p26-q4, where the domain comes directly from the simplified expression. It is below p20-q25, which also asks the student to decide which composite does not exist.
